policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV explicitly has 'another strong angel,' requiring ἄλλον and excluding its omission.
ASV 'upon his head' can render either the accusative τὴν κεφαλὴν or genitive τῆς κεφαλῆς after ἐπί; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'a little book' reflects diminutive βιβλαρίδιον rather than βιβλίον 'book'.
ASV 'sware by him that liveth' can render either the bare dative construction or the reading with inserted ἐν; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'his servants' does not distinguish reflexive ἑαυτοῦ before δούλους from personal αὐτοῦ after it; retain the base fallback.
ASV relative syntax 'the voice which I heard ... speaking with me' does not expose whether the participle is accusative λαλοῦσαν or nominative λαλοῦσα; retain the base fallback.
ASV relative syntax does not expose whether 'saying' is accusative λέγουσαν or nominative λέγουσα; retain the base fallback.
ASV calls this item 'the book,' distinguishing βιβλίον from diminutive βιβλιδάριον; compare its 'little book' in verses 2, 9, and 10.
ASV 'I went' does not distinguish the first-aorist form ἀπῆλθα from the second-aorist form ἀπῆλθον; retain the base fallback.
Both diminutives βιβλαρίδιον and βιβλιδάριον are compatible with ASV 'the little book'; retain the base fallback.
ASV 'the little book' reflects diminutive βιβλαρίδιον rather than βιβλίον 'book'.
ASV's single 'over' may govern the entire coordinated list whether or not ἐπί is repeated before the final member; retain the base fallback.
